subject: Non convergence in MGCFA with original vars and convergence with vars corrected for covariates

messages.author: 8067f4c0eecf7ba8
messages.subject: Non convergence in MGCFA with original vars and convergence with vars corrected for covariates
parts:
Dear all, 

In my current analysis, I'm running through a problem. In one of my MGCFA models, using the original cognitive subtest variables, I got the error message "lavaan WARNING: model has NOT converged!" whereas when I correct for age and gender effects, the model has converged. I have no idea what happened and how to interpret this outcome.

Here's what the syntax looks like :


setwd("c:\\Users\\R") 
entiredata<-read.csv("Woodcock-Johnson Murray_2007.csv")

require(lavaan)
require(psy)

entiredata3<- subset(entiredata, racesample<3 & wj==3 & sample==1)
require(dplyr)
d3<- select(entiredata3, testage, sex, racesample, sample, wj, c02spatrels, c04visaudit, c05blend, c06verbcomp, c07vismatch, c09analsyn, c10numrev, c11concform, c13picrecog, c14memwords, c15geninfo, c16retrieve, c17audatten, c18decisions)
d3 = d3[complete.cases(d3),] 

m1<- lm(c02spatrels~ testage+sex, data=d3, weights=d3$weight)
d3$spatrels<-residuals(m1)
m2<- lm(c04visaudit~ testage+sex, data=d3, weights=d3$weight)
d3$visaudit<-residuals(m2)
m3<- lm(c05blend~ testage+sex, data=d3, weights=d3$weight)
d3$blend<-residuals(m3)
m4<- lm(c06verbcomp~ testage+sex, data=d3, weights=d3$weight)
d3$verbcomp<-residuals(m4)
m5<- lm(c07vismatch~ testage+sex, data=d3, weights=d3$weight)
d3$vismatch<-residuals(m5)
m6<- lm(c09analsyn~ testage+sex, data=d3, weights=d3$weight)
d3$analsyn<-residuals(m6)
m7<- lm(c10numrev~ testage+sex, data=d3, weights=d3$weight)
d3$numrev<-residuals(m7)
m8<- lm(c11concform~ testage+sex, data=d3, weights=d3$weight)
d3$concform<-residuals(m8)
m9<- lm(c13picrecog~ testage+sex, data=d3, weights=d3$weight)
d3$picrecog<-residuals(m9)
m10<- lm(c14memwords~ testage+sex, data=d3, weights=d3$weight)
d3$memwords<-residuals(m10)
m11<- lm(c15geninfo~ testage+sex, data=d3, weights=d3$weight)
d3$geninfo<-residuals(m11)
m12<- lm(c16retrieve~ testage+sex, data=d3, weights=d3$weight)
d3$retrieve<-residuals(m12)
m13<- lm(c17audatten~ testage+sex, data=d3, weights=d3$weight)
d3$audatten<-residuals(m13)
m14<- lm(c18decisions~ testage+sex, data=d3, weights=d3$weight)
d3$decisions<-residuals(m14)

dgroup3<-select(d3, racesample, sample, wj, spatrels, visaudit, blend, verbcomp, vismatch, analsyn, numrev, concform, picrecog, memwords, geninfo, retrieve, audatten, decisions)

combined.commonfactor14.model <-'
Gc =~ c06verbcomp + c15geninfo  
Gf =~ c02spatrels + c04visaudit + c09analsyn + c11concform + c13picrecog 
Gsm =~ c05blend + c10numrev + c14memwords 
Gs=~ c07vismatch + c16retrieve + c17audatten + c18decisions 
Gs ~ 0*1
'

commonfactor14.fit<-cfa(combined.commonfactor14.model, data=d3, group="racesample", meanstructure=TRUE, group.equal=c("loadings", "intercepts", "residuals", "lv.variances", "lv.covariances"), group.partial=c("Gc~~Gc", "Gf~~Gf", "Gsm~~Gsm", "Gc~~Gf", "Gc~~Gsm", "Gf~~Gsm"))
fitMeasures(commonfactor14.fit, c("chisq", "df", "pvalue", "cfi", "rmsea", "srmr", "aic", "bic"))

combined.commonfactor14.model <-'
Gc =~ verbcomp + geninfo 
Gf =~ spatrels + visaudit + analsyn + concform + picrecog 
Gsm =~ blend + numrev + memwords 
Gs =~ vismatch + retrieve + audatten + decisions 
Gs ~ 0*1
'

commonfactor14.fit<-cfa(combined.commonfactor14.model, data=dgroup3, group="racesample", meanstructure=TRUE, group.equal=c("loadings", "intercepts", "residuals", "lv.variances", "lv.covariances"), group.partial=c("Gc~~Gc", "Gf~~Gf", "Gsm~~Gsm", "Gc~~Gf", "Gc~~Gsm", "Gf~~Gsm"))
fitMeasures(commonfactor14.fit, c("chisq", "df", "pvalue", "cfi", "rmsea", "srmr", "aic", "bic"))

It's also curious that the model fit among other models are very close when using uncorrected variables compared to when using corrected variables.

Any help is appreciated.

Thanks in advance.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Non convergence in MGCFA with original vars and convergence with vars corrected for covariates
parts:
I have no idea what is going on, but a couple oddities I noticed:
  • You don't seem to select() a "weight" variable when you create d3, but you use it in your lm() calls.  Is that a sampling weight that needs to be accounted for in your CFA, too?  If so, look into the lavaan.survey package.
  • You are fitting a highly restrictive model.  Have you fit a configural model to see if it converges when you allow estimates to differ across groups?  Typically, those measurement-invariance constraints are sequentially tested one set at a time, to make sure those assumptions hold.  Look into the measurementInvariance() function in the semTools package.
  • Instead of running 14 regressions, you could (and maybe should) regress the indicators on age and sex in your CFA.  The way you are doing it assumes that the effects of age and sex are constant across the groups in your CFA, which might not be the case.  Including those controls in your CFA would allow you to test the assumption that they are equivalent by including "regressions" in your group.equal argument and testing whether model fit is worse.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.subject: Re: Non convergence in MGCFA with original vars and convergence with vars corrected for covariates
parts: 3. I may want to test invariance in these cognitive subtests after partialling out age and gender effect. Do you know how I should write the syntax using group.equal and regression ?

Use the regression operator "~" in your model syntax, for example:

c06verbcomp + c15geninfo ... + audatten + decisions ~ testage + sex

Then just add "regressions" to the vector along with "loadings", "intercepts", and all the others.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Non convergence in MGCFA with original vars and convergence with vars corrected for covariates
parts:
Is the syntax correct?

Yes

I have compared the output with the model syntax that does not include testage and sex variables as covariates, and the former model fits the data better. So, I suppose I have to conclude that gender and age effects don't matter at all in group differences.

Well, that is the wrong conclusion because the models are not fit to the same data if they don't include the same variables.  First, you wanted to control for the effects of age and sex, so you don't need to compare model fit between models with and without them.  If you want to know whether age and sex have significant effects, look at the tests and effect sizes of those regression coefficients.  Second, in addition to the model you ran, you should also fit the model (i.e., using the same syntax) without including "regressions" in the "group.equal" vector.  Then, use anova() to compare the fit of those nested models to test your assumption that those regression coefficients are equal across groups.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
